newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says paid $608 million in medical arrears.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says paid $608 million in medical arrears.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has paid around 2.28 billion riyals ($608 million) in arrears and current dues to suppliers and Health Ministry personnel, Health Minister Osama bin Abdul-Majid Shobokshi was on Wednesday quoted as saying.
Saudi newspapers quoted the minister as saying more than 1.02 billion riyals were paid for commitments arising in previous years and more than 1.24 billion for this year's dues.
The minister did not say if or how much the ministry still owed in arrears, which industry sources say had been accumulating since at least 1993.

The sources and bankers in the kingdom said in August that Saudi Arabia, one of the Middle East's top pharmaceutical consumers, had started paying part of hundreds of millions of dollars in arrears to international suppliers.

Some of the biggest European and U.S. companies had been pressing the Health Ministry to settle the arrears to foreign suppliers, estimated at $1 billion. Bankers estimate total ministry arrears at between $2 billion and $3 billion.
They say the government had decided to pay some Health Ministry arrears at a rate of 20 percent per year over five years in cash.

In 1995 Riyadh began issuing special bonds to make a dent in the estimated $5 billion outstanding to contractors. It has also issued special certificates to farmers estimated to be worth nine billion riyals.

The debt had been mounting since the early 1990s as a result of huge Gulf War liabilities amid weak world oil prices. Saudi Arabia -- the world's largest oil producer and exporter -- is estimated to have earned around $10 billion more than it had budgeted this year due to higher oil prices.
